messages:
maria: Quick sync — we need a short decision on whether to accept quantized model binaries into the registry as first-class artifacts.
ben: Are we talking .pt/q4/q8 binaries that people produce from local quantization runs?
maria: Yeah. The ask is: allow teams to upload quantized checkpoints and treat them as valid for onboarding (bench + smoke).
jordan: Pros: much cheaper to run in Dedicated/private, faster perf tests. Cons: can hide correctness regressions vs fp32 baseline.
ali: We framed this in onboarding smoke vs full bench. If we accept quantized, we should force a short dequantization parity check in the bench. e.g. run 100 golden prompts and assert token-level diffs under threshold.
ben: I worry about flaky diffs due to nondeterminism. Might need golden sampling seeds and deterministic kernels for the parity check.
maria: Agreed. Proposal: require two artifacts on upload: (1) the quantized binary, (2) a small canonical float baseline (maybe trimmed to smaller size). Upload validation runs: smoke (latency, sanity), and parity-run (deterministic seeds). If parity fails, block onboard.
jordan: How strict should parity be? Exact token equality is unrealistic for q4. Suggest BLEU-ish / n-gram overlap threshold + a targeted hallucination check.
ali: Also require a signing header metadata field: quantization recipe + tooling version (e.g., bitsandbytes v0.40, clamp options). That helps debug mismatches.
ben: Storage/cost: storing both float baseline and quantized bump storage. Maybe we allow compressed baseline or reference snapshot stored externally (s3 url).
maria: We can allow an external baseline URL but require the registry to fetch it during validation. For air-gapped private deployments, we need an option to supply the baseline in the package.
sre-bot: deploybot: Note — any upload longer than 500MB will trigger async validation and email the uploader once finished.
jordan: Fallback behavior: if quantized artifact passes smoke but fails parity, we should still allow a soft-approve for internal dev but block public/dedicated rollout.
ali: +1. Add a flag on the registry named "quanted_trust_level": [dev, internal, approved]. Default dev.
ben: One more thing: bench metrics must include a quality delta column showing parity score and a commit tag of quantization-recipe. This will feed Optimize tooling for recommendations.
maria: Action items: I’ll draft a short gating doc with: required metadata fields, parity test spec (seeded 100 cases, scoring function), allowed trust levels, and storage options. @ben can you sketch an example metadata schema? @jordan can you propose a scoring threshold to start with (~0.85 n-gram overlap?)
ben: Will do. Quick example:
```
quant.meta = {
  "q_bits": "4",
  "tool": "bitsandbytes",
  "tool_version": "0.40",
  "recipe": "perchannel-clamp",
  "baseline_url": "s3://redwood-registry/baselines/llama-2-7b-fp32.tar.gz",
  "trust_level": "dev"
}
```
jordan: I can prototype the scoring harness next week. Start with n-gram overlap + perplexity delta guard rails.
ali: If anyone is OOO, ping me; I’ll collect comments into the RFC follow-up. :+1:
maria: Thanks — landing doc by Fri EOD. If folks want to bike-shed parity metric, do it in the doc thread.
ben: ack
jordan: ack
ali: ack
